title: Embracing the future of Artificial Intelligence in the classroom: the relevance of AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking in modern education
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper discusses the growing role of artificial intelligence in education, with a focus on three key competencies: AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical thinking. The central question is how schools and universities should respond to the rapid adoption of tools such as ChatGPT, especially given concerns about hallucinations, plagiarism, overreliance on AI, and uneven knowledge among students and staff.

The paper combines a conceptual discussion with a case study from Kalaidos University of Applied Sciences in Zurich, Switzerland, and a narrative literature review. The case study describes how the institution developed internal AI guidelines for written work, requiring transparency about which AI tools were used, how they were used, how outputs were critically evaluated, and where AI contributed to the manuscript. The paper also surveys classroom uses of AI such as experimentation with chatbots, case-study generation, curriculum design support, gamification, and immersive technologies.

The paper argues that simply banning or unrestrictedly allowing AI is inadequate. Instead, it recommends building an AI culture through workshops, regular updates, budgets for training, dedicated staff positions, and explicit AI literacy education. It further presents prompt engineering as a pedagogical tool and argues that students should learn to use AI as a sparring partner rather than a ghostwriter or tutor. Overall, the paper is a position piece aimed primarily at higher education, though it suggests the ideas may also be useful more broadly.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual discussion paper with a narrative literature review and anecdotal case material, not a controlled empirical study. It does not present a testable design, outcome estimates, or causal identification.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not report direct empirical impact on student learning outcomes or institutional performance. Its contributions are framing and recommendations, so measurable educational impact is unclear.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual discussion of ChatGPT and other large language models as educational tools, including using them as a 'sparring partner' for brainstorming, case generation, curriculum support, and guided classroom interaction rather than as a tutor or ghostwriter.

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that structured use of ChatGPT/LLMs, prompt engineering, and AI literacy can strengthen students' critical thinking and reflective evaluation of AI outputs. No experimental estimate is reported; the claim is supported by conceptual argument and examples such as prompting students to critique AI-generated answers and verify them against literature.
finding.measure: Critical thinking, reflective evaluation of AI outputs, and prompt-engineering competency

finding.finding_summary: The paper proposes institutional AI guidelines, workshops, curricula changes, and dedicated staffing/budget as mechanisms to improve responsible AI adoption in schools and universities. This is a conceptual recommendation paper, so no quantitative institutional effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Institutional policy/guideline development and AI-governance practices

finding.finding_summary: The article suggests that LLMs can help teachers and students save time on tasks such as curriculum design, case-study creation, brainstorming, and other writing support. These efficiency claims are illustrative rather than empirically tested, and no sample size or effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Teacher workload reduction and task efficiency in planning/writing support
